reviews.headline: Kompany returns but Kane limps off as Bayern Munich held by Cologne in Bundesliga
reviews.quote: Both sides had chances in a busy second half but it remained goalless and the point was enough for Bayern to edge a point ahead of Borussia Dortmund.

title_options: Bayern had the ball. Köln had the chances.
Why Kompany said Köln deserved the draw
script.description:
Bayern München 1-1 1. FC Köln, Bundesliga round 10. Bayern had most of the ball and 17 shots, yet the chances were worth more to Köln. We follow Kompany's return, Wagner's plan for fast breaks, one save at minute 51, and what expected goals say about who deserved more. Sources for quotes: Bundesliga.com, FC Bayern, Geissblog.koeln, ran (Joyn), AP via Yahoo Sports, Sportschau (ARD), AFP via Malay Mail, and StatsBomb open data for the history comparison.

Tell us in the comments: was the draw fair? Data: FotMob.

shots.text: Allianz Arena, Munich. A Friday night in the Bundesliga, round 10. Four weeks ago, Vincent Kompany collapsed at Bayern's training ground. He spent five days in hospital, then went home to rest. While he was away, his assistant Aaron Danks took the team for five matches: four wins and a draw. Tonight, Kompany is back on the touchline.
Their visitors, 1. FC Köln, have won one of their last five, and lost two. The final score is 1-1.
But a 1-1 can hide a very different story. Who really controlled this match... and who should have won it?

shots.text: Going in, the form was lopsided. Bayern: four wins and a draw, including 2-0 away at Atlético Madrid. Köln: one win, two draws, two defeats, the latest a 1-2 loss at home to Bayer Leverkusen.

Köln's coach is René Wagner, 37, in his first job as a head coach. For years he was Steffen Baumgart's assistant. He took over in March, when Lukas Kwasniok was sacked, kept Köln up, and was given the job until 2028. In the FC Bayern preview he asked: "Other teams have already taken points off them in Munich – so why not us?" His plan, per Geissblog.koeln: fast transitions, and expect Bayern to push them back.

visual.speaker: René Wagner

shots.text: Both were short of players. Bayern were without Luis Díaz, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry. Köln were without five, including Thijs Dallinga.

shots.text: Allianz Arena. Minute 12. Köln break.
Saïd El Mala finds Mikey Moore. Moore finishes with his right foot. 0-1. This is the fast break Wagner described.
Bayern answer by taking over. By FotMob's momentum measure, they are on top for 83 percent of the first half.
Minute 37. Tom Bischof's pass, and Nathaniel Brown scores with his left foot, from open play. 1-1. But the level score hides a bigger imbalance.

shots.text: Minute 51. Köln break again. Moore shoots from inside the box, and Jonas Urbig saves.
A goal here makes it 1-2. Urbig makes 3 saves in the match, 2 of them diving, and each one keeps the score level.
Our reading: this is where the match could have tipped. The turning point is not a goal. It is a save.

shots.text: After the break, Bayern keep pushing and Köln keep defending. Jonathan Tah, the highest-rated starter, wins all 4 of his ground duels.
Harry Kane is the lowest-rated Bayern starter. But he was substituted after only 9 touches, so it is a short sample, not a verdict.
Bayern keep 72 percent of the ball. Köln make 32 tackles to their 14. That points to a side happy to defend, then break.

shots.text: Now the part the score hides. Expected goals, or xG, is a model built on many past shots: distance, angle, foot or head, type of pass. It says how often a chance like that is scored.
FotMob gives Köln 1.99 xG and Bayern 1.07. Every Köln shot came from inside the box. Most of Bayern's 17 did not.
Köln then missed 3 of their 4 big chances. Urbig saved 0.63 goals more than an average keeper would. Our reading: the draw owes something to Köln's finishing and something to Bayern's goalkeeper.
Replay these chances 20,000 times, and Köln win 64 of every 100. Bayern win 14.

shorts.title: Jonathan Tah: best rated, in a 1-1 draw

shots.text: Jonathan Tah scored nothing, and still got the best rating of the night: 8.3.
He won all 4 of his ground duels. He also made 6 defensive actions and 2 clearances.
On the ball he was just as tidy: 65 of 68 passes found a team-mate, 9 of them into the final third.
Bayern were on top in 83% of first-half minutes and 70% of the second. Tah's calm passing fitted that control.
The rating cannot show everything, though. Köln still scored at minute 12 and the match ended 1-1. Is a defender's 8.3 enough on a night like that? Full story on the channel.

shorts.title: Köln's fast breaks should have won it
shorts.hook: Two breaks. One goal. One point.

shots.text: Bayern had 72% of the ball, but Köln had the better chances.
Minute 12: Saïd El Mala, 20, named in Germany's World Cup squad this summer, sets up Mikey Moore on a fast break, and Köln lead 1-0.
Minute 51: another break, Moore again, and Jonas Urbig saves it. Moore's two shots were worth 1.43 expected goals, which is what an average finisher would score from them.
Köln's chances added up to 1.99 expected goals, all from open play. Bayern's added up to 1.07. Replayed 20,000 times, Köln win 64%.
Kompany said Köln deserved the result. Can a team with 28% of the ball keep doing this? Full story on the channel.
